title: Price floor sensitivity and ops butterfly plan
content:
Purpose
Draft playbook to operationalize a price-floor sensitivity strategy paired with an "ops butterfly" (short-term capacity swaps + crediting protocol) to protect runway and SLA performance during potential price compression events. This doc codifies triggers, an incremental headcount contingency, and a partner credit allocation for mid- and near-term scenarios.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Root problem: token price erosion risk and potential margin squeeze over next 6–12 months; need a low-friction mechanical response that preserves core SLAs without immediate large-scale layoffs.
- Proposed construct: a three-tiered response that (1) sets a temporary internal price floor for new enterprise quotes, (2) funds a small partner-credit pool to absorb strategic uptake, and (3) implements an "ops butterfly" headcount buffer (contractors + short-term redeployments) to flex capacity without permanent HC changes.
- Outcome goal: protect 3 months of runway margin at current burn + avoid >10% degradation to P95 latency for top-10 customers.

Assumptions used for sensitivity model
- Current blended token margin: 62% at current price bands (hosted API + some dedicated).
- Average enterprise contract latency headroom: 18% before needing dedicated capacity.
- Contractor fully-burdened rate used for surge: $11,000/month (GPU-side ops + infra allocation).
- Token demand growth scenarios: flat / +20% / -15% over 6 months.
- Price shock scenarios modeled: -30% / -15% / 0% / +10% relative to current per-token price.

Scenario matrix (simple excerpt)
Scenario | Demand delta | Price delta | Estimated margin
Baseline | 0% | 0% | 62%
Soft shock | +20% | -15% | 47%
Deep shock | +20% | -30% | 32%
Downside demand | -15% | -15% | 52%
Upside price | +20% | +10% | 70%

(Full simulation linked in github PR; this doc contains ops triggers and HC plan.)

Ops Butterfly construct (why "butterfly")
- Two short wings (contractor surge + partner credits) cushion the shoulders of a central action (temporary hold on new mid-market discounts + limited hiring freeze for ICs). The idea is to shift cost exposure away from fixed payroll and into variable, reversible instruments.

Concrete levers and sequencing
1) Immediate (0–30 days)
   - Set internal quoting floor: finance approves a temporary minimum effective price (M = current price * 0.85) for any new multi-month enterprise deals. Sales notified via Slack thread and a short Confluence FAQ.
   - Partner-credit pool: carve $1.2M (initial) from contingency to issue credits to top-channel partners to maintain renewals and avoid churn while pricing is re-calibrated. Credits require VP-level signoff.
   - Hiring freeze on non-customer-facing roles (rolling 8-week reconsider cadence). Exceptions via People Ops + hiring committee.

2) Near-term (30–90 days)
   - Contractor ops surge: up to +18 FTE-equivalent contractors in SRE/infra/serving runtime for burst windows. Prioritize contractors with GPU ops experience. Contractor window cap: 90 days (renewable once).
   - Quantization rollout acceleration: product/infra 60-day sprint to expand quant profiles on mid-tier models to reduce GPU cost by ~12% per token on targeted workloads. Engineering sprint tracked under JIRA: FIN-7242 / INFRA-5031.
   - Pricing experiments: run two controlled offers (A/B) for price floor vs. market-reflective price to gauge churn sensitivity for top-30 customers. Document in GH sim PR and sales notes.

3) Medium-term (90–180 days)
   - Convert effective contractor capacity into either permanent roles or terminate depending on demand signal (decision hinge at 120 days). Decision criteria: 8-week rolling average token throughput, top-10 customer retention, and margin trajectory.
   - Partner-credit repayment / amortization plan: credits must be expensed over 6 months; any unused credits returned to contingency.

Headcount contingency plan (HC detail)
- Zero baseline: no involuntary layoffs in this plan unless a scenario beyond Deep shock occurs.
- Contingency pool composition (quick listing):
   - SRE/infra contractors: up to 12 FTE-eq (priority)
   - Customer success temporary hires: up to 6 for renewal push
   - Product ops temporary reprioritization: move 4 ICs for quantization sprint (60 days)
- Cost accounting: contractor pool funded from contingency; if extended > 120 days shift to hiring funnel with interview target and OTE adjustments.

Pricing sensitivity: quick mappings (estimates)
- 15% price compression with flat demand -> margin loss ~15 percentage points; runway reduction ~3–4 weeks at current burn.
- 30% compression + +20% demand -> margin loss ~30 percentage points; immediate need to activate full butterfly (credits + contractors + aggressive quantization).
- Sensitivity to churn: a 5% increase in churn among top-50 customers multiplies revenue deterioration by ~1.4x because of higher ACV concentration.

Governance & triggers
- Trigger 1 (amber): 12-week rolling unit margin drops >8pp -> stand up Pricing Ops daily standup, notify CFO and Head of Sales.
- Trigger 2 (red): 6-week rolling margin drops >18pp OR two top-10 renewals churn -> execute partner-credit distribution and contractor surge (deploy contractors within 7 business days).
- All triggers write to an incident board (Operations: FIN-INC-2026-06).

Communication plan
- Internal: ops playbook + FAQ posted to Confluence; short slide deck to Exec (5 slides) summarizing triggers and next steps.
- External: coordinated partner comms if credits are used; Sales to include a 1-paragraph note in customer renewal decks when relevant.

Open questions / risks (notes to execs)
- Reputational risk of frequent credits to partners (long-term discount expectations).
- Contractor ramp quality: hardware ops ramp time measured at ~10–12 days; plan buffer accordingly.
- Quantization rollback risk: quality regressions on certain prompt families; must maintain a small eval set and gating.

Next steps (owner: Ava Chen)
- Align CFO + Legal on partner-credit term template by 2026-05-20.
- Prioritize contractor bench candidates and confirm initial 6 on-call contractors by 2026-05-28 (owner: Diego Ramos).
- Link full simulation outputs in the GH PR for iterative modeling (owner: Maya Patel).

Notes to self: keep this doc purposefully concise; append model outputs and a cleaned sprint checklist once decisions are green-lit.

-- end --
